Andhra Pradesh

Trick to Remember: Veer Logon Ke Liye Dhimese Koyle Ki Bhaap Se Burra Banalu

TrickDance
VeerVeeranatyam (Dance of Braves) Performed by Veeramusti community [believed to be followers of Veerabhadra (Lord Shiva)]
LogonLambadi: Banjara tribe
DhimeseDhimsa (tribe of Araku valley) Performed by 15-20 women forming a chain
KoyleKolattam
BhaapBhamakalapam (dance-drama) Composed by Sidhyendra Yogi
BurraBurrakatha
BanaluBonalu: Celebrated in honour of Goddess Mahakali. Butta Bommalu (mask dance) Performed in West Godavari region. Butta Bommalu means "Basket Toys". Dappu Nrityam

Arunachal Pradesh

Trick to Remember: Rekha → Aruna Aji Wancho Baua Ke Pas Chalo Sham Ko Aur Mask Lagake Lion and Peacock Dance Dekho

TrickDance
RekhaRikhampada: Mishmi tribe
AjiAji Lamu: Monpa tribe
WanchoWancho: Wancho tribe. Celebrated in March/April during Oriah festival
Baua Ke PasBuiya: Digaru Mishmi tribe. Pasi Kongki: Adi tribe performs this on Abhang songs
ChaloChalo Loku: Nocte tribe performs in Oct-Nov. Bardo Chham: Dance of 12 zodiacs (Sherdukpen community) and is associated with Tibetan-Buddhist
Sham KoSham
MaskMask
Lion and PeacockLion and Peacock: Monpa tribe. Popir: Performed by Garo tribe in tribute to Mopin Ape (Goddess of prosperity and fertility). Ponung: Adi tribe. Yak Chham Dance (mask dance) It is also known as Yak dance

Assam

Trick to Remember: Ali Bhor Main Deo Ke Pass Gaya, Hey Bhagawan Maths Main Ank Dila Dena Iss Pali Main Jhum Ke Nachunga

TrickDance
AliAli ai Ligang: Mishimi tribe performs Gumrag dance in this festival (observed on first Wednesday of Feb-March)
BhorBhortal: Developed by Narhari Burha Bhakat and is performed by Satriya community in Barpeta
DeoDeodhani: Performed to pay tribute to Goddess Mansa (Snake Goddess)
AnkAnkiya Naat (one-act play) It is centred around acts of Lord Krishna and teachings of Vaishnavite faith
PaliOjapali: Semi-dramatic tradition folk dance
JhumJhumur: Performed by Kulis (people who work in tea gardens). Bagarumba: Performed by Bodo tribe during Bwisaga festival (women wear Dokhona/Arunai). Bihu: It is a dance and also a festival. Baidima: Dimasa tribe. Bawang: Karbi Anglong tribe

Bihar

Trick to Remember: Do Natwe Jat-Jatin Apna Sohar Khila Rahe Hai Jhum Ke

TrickDance
NatweNatwa: Chamar community
Jat JatinJat-Jatin: Shows tragic lovestory of Jat and Jatin. It is performed in Mithila region during moonlit nights (monsoon)
Sohar KhilaSohar Khelwana: Performed during child birth
Jhum KeJhumeri: Performed in Mithilanchal region during Karthik month (Oct-Nov)

Bidesia: Dance based on social issue of society. Bamar: Julaha community. Jhijhiya (Mithila region) Women balance lanterns while balancing this dance. Kajari: Performed during monsoon season. Purka dance, Dhibia dance.

Chhattisgarh

Trick to Remember: Aksar Suwa Karma Na Karke Gendiya Marte Hai Pagalpanti Karte Hai Aur Pandavo Ke Saath Jhumur Ke Niche Saila Dance Karte Hai

TrickDance
AksarKaksar: Abujhmaria tribe of Bastar region
SuwaSuwa Nacha (Parrot Dance) Kamar tribe
KarmaKarma Nacha: Performed during Karma festival around sacred Karma tree
GendiyaGendi: Baiga tribe
Marte HaiGaur Maria
PagalpantiPanthi Nacha: Performed by Satnami community (followers of Satnam panth)
PandavoPandavani: A style of folk singing which includes narration of tales from Mahabharata
JhumurJhumair
Saila DanceSaila: Performed by boys of Bhil tribe during harvest season

Famous Exponents of Pandavani Dance: Usha Barle (Padma Shri in 2023) and Teejan Bai (Padma Vibhushan in 2019).

Gujarat

Trick to Remember: Gujarat Ki Gopiyan Dandiya aur Garba Khelne Siddiyon Se Matak Ke Padhar Rahi Hai

TrickDance
GopiyanGop Raas
DandiyaDandiya Raas: The dance depicts fight between Durga Mate and Mahisasura. It is performed during Navratri after aarti
GarbaGarba: Graceful dance performed during Navratri before aarti
Siddiyon SeSiddhi Dhamal: Siddhi community
MatakMatukadi: Ravari and Bharwad community
PadharPadhar: Padhar community. Tippani: Koli and Kharwa tribe (Chorwad district). Hudo: Bharwad tribe (shepherd community). Bhavai. Lasya. Vinchiudo

Goa

Trick to Remember: Mandvi Ghode Gadi Jaguar Dekhne Aur Patang Udane Goa Ja Rahi Hai. Chalo Gaon Romat So Jao Jake

TrickDance
MandviMando: This dance depicts love and romance
GhodeGhode Modnhi: This dance depicts bravery and victory and honours Maratha warriors
GadiTalgadi, Fugdi (celebrated during Ganesh Chathurthi)
JaguarJagor: This dance starts at midnight and continues till early morning
DekhneDekhni: Performed by Christian girls wearing Indian attire in a music that is a blend of Indian melody and Western rhythm
PatangTarangmel: Performed during Holi and Dussehra festivals
GoaGoa
ChaloDhalo: Performed by women standing in two parallel rows interlocking their arms
GaonGonf: Performed during festivals after the harvest
RomatRomat: The dance is associated with Shigmo festival in the month of Phalgun (Feb-March)
So JaoSao Jao: Performed during Sao Jao festivals in the month of June. Kunbi

Himachal Pradesh

Trick to Remember: Nata Chhora Aman Him Pe Rakshasno Ka Chola Aur Mala Odh Ke Sandh Per Baithkar Dang Lekar Chapa Chap Kar Raha Hai

TrickDance
NataNati: The dance holds Guinness World Record for the most number of dancers (9,892 dancers) participating in Kullu district
ChhoraJhora/Jhali
AmanDhaman: Performed during Dussehra in Kullu region
Him PeHimachal Pradesh
RakshasnoRakshas Nritya: Performed wearing a demon mask
CholaCholamba: Oldest dance performed after killing a tiger
MalaKayang Mala: Performed by boys and girls who form a garland-like pattern by interlocking their arms
SandhShand/Shabu: Performed mainly in Buddhist monasteries and Lahaul
DangDangi
ChapaChapeli: Performed in Sirmour and Chamba districts
ChapChham: Performed by Buddhist monks to ward off evil spirits. Rasa: Performed in Sirmour district

Haryana

Trick to Remember: Haryana Ki Choriya Daphli aur Manjira Leke Jhumar Ke Niche Dhamaal Macha Rahe Phalgun Main

TrickDance
ChoriyaKhoria: This dance is a variety of Jhumar dance style
DaphliDaph: Performed in spring season to commemorate bountiful harvest
ManjiraManjira: Performed in Mewat district
JhumarJhumar: Performed by young married girls
DhamaalDhamaal: Performed by men of Ahir community outside in moonlight (in Phalgun). The origin of dance is rooted back to Mahabharata
PhalgunPhag: Performed in Phalgun during Holi. Loor: Performed by girls of Bangar region in Phalgun during Holi. Saang: A popular folk theatre dance. Gugga: Performed by men in loving memory of Saint Gugga

Jammu & Kashmir

Trick to Remember: Harris Rouf Bhand Hoke Dhul Main Kud Raha Hai Manali Main

TrickDance
Harris RoufRouf: Performed by women in standing in rows during Eid/Ramadan (in spring)
BhandBhand Pather: It is a dance-drama
DhulDumhal: Performed by men of Wattal tribe
KudKud: Performed at night to honour Lok Devta
HaiHikat: Performed in spring in harvest season. Participants join hands and spin while singing
ManaliDamali

Jharkhand

  • Karam/Karma Dance: Performed by Oraon tribe where they worship Kadam tree during the festival (autumnal festival).
  • Paika Dance: It is a traditional martial art dance performed by Munda tribe or Sadar community.
  • Mundari Dance: A traditional tribal dance of the Munda community performed during harvest festivals.

(continued Jharkhand and other dances)

  • Domkach Dance: It is a Nagpuri folk dance.
  • Jhummar Dance: It is a folk dance performed by Sadan community.
  • Chhau Dance: It is a martial art dance → Three types: Purulia Chhau (West Bengal), Seraikella (Jharkhand), and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).
  • Santhali Dance: This dance is also known as Jhika Dasain and is performed in October month by Santhal tribe.
  • Hunta Dance: An ancient tribal dance performed by Santhal tribe which is a form of preparation for hunting.
  • Phagua Dance.

Karnataka

Trick to Remember: Yash Bola Kam Kar Saale Doll Bhootha Nagamandali Veerta Khatam Karegi

TrickDance
YashYakshagana: Performed in colourful dresses in coastal regions. Yakshagana meaning "song of the celestial beings"
BolaBolak
KamKamsale: Performed by devotees of God Mahadeshwara. Kamsale is a brass instrument
KarKarga
DollDollu Kunitha (drum-dance) Performed by Kuruba community. Dollu means "drum" in Kannada
BhoothaBhootha Aradhne: A ritualistic dance performed in coastal regions to celebrate connection between human, nature and divine spirit
NagmandaliNagamandala: Performed by two priests, one enacts male snake and other as female snake
VeertaVeeragase: Performed by Virabhadra community during Dussehra

Kerala

  • Ottamthullal Dance: A dance-drama was introduced by Kunchan Nambiar.
  • Kaliyattam Dance: It is also known as Theyyam and depicts religious rituals of sacred grooves of Malabar coast.
  • Koodiyattam Dance: This dance is a traditional Sanskrit theatre art dance.
  • Kolakali Dance: In this dance, the dancers move in a circle striking small sticks in rhythm with their steps.
  • Chakyar Koothu: A monologue performance where the performer narrates episodes from Hindu epics (such as Ramayana and Mahabharata).
  • Thappukali Dance, Kooravarakali Dance, Thiruvarakali Dance.

Madhya Pradesh

Trick to Remember: Aksar Goriya Ada Dikhane Ke Liye Matki Main Jawara Aur Phulpati Rakhke Manch Pe Khada Nachti Hai Aur Tali Bajati Hai

TrickDance
AksarKaksar: Abujhmaria or Muria tribe of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh
GoriyaBhagoria: Bhil tribe of Jhabua district
AdaAada: The dance is variation of matki dance performed in Malwa region
MatkiMatki: Performed in Malwa region
JawaraJawara: Harvest dance
PhulpatiPhulpati: Performed by unmarried girls of Malwa region
ManchMaach: Performed in Malwa region
Khada NachtiKhada Nach
TaliTertali: Kamar tribe. Saila: Performed during Dussehra

Manipur

  • Thang-Ta Dance: Manipuri martial art dance.
  • Lai Haraoba Dance: Meitei tribe.
  • Dhol Cholom: Drum-dance performed during Holi.
  • Pung Cholom: This dance is also known as Mridanga kirtan or Dhumal.
  • Jagoi Dance: This dance is also known as Manipuri Raasleela.
  • Khamba Thoibi Dance: Meitei tribe.
  • Nupa Dance.

Meghalaya

  • Nongkrem Dance: Khasi tribe.
  • Wangala Dance: Performed by Garo tribe during Wangala festival (also known as "Festival of Hundred Drums").
  • Behdeinkhalam Dance: Jaintia tribe.
  • Laho Dance: Jaintia tribe.
  • Shad Suk Mynsiem: Khasi tribe.

Mizoram

Trick to Remember: Mizoram Ke Manch Pe Khullam Chillam Zang Chal Rahi

TrickDance
KhullamKhullam: It is also known as "Dance of Guests"
ChillamChailam: Performed during Chapchar Kut festival
ZangZangtalam: Paite tribe
ChalCheraw: This dance is also known as Bamboo dance. Chheihlam

Maharashtra

Trick to Remember: Ek Kohli Vadapav Lana, Lazy Kahin Ki Tamasha Kar Rahi Hai, Dafa Hoja Varna Mouni Jo Dhangka Natak Karti Hai Uske Paas Chala Jaunga

TrickDance
KohliKoli: Performed by fisherman community
VadapavPovadas: The dance describes events in life of Chhatrapati Shivaji
LanaLavani: A combination of traditional song and dance performed to the beats of Dholki
LazyLezim: An acrobatic dance that involves calisthenic moves
TamashaTamasha: It is derived from Sanskrit drama "Prahsana" and "Bhana"
DafaGafa: Performed by Gond tribe in Vidharbha region
MouniMouni
DhangkaDhangari: Performed by shepherds, cowheards and blanket weavers of Sholapur district (known as Dhangars)
NatakNatak
  • Baithakichi Lavani: Lavani performed for a private audience.
  • Sulochna Chavan is known as Lavani Samradhni (Lavani Queen).

Nagaland

Trick to Remember: Nagaland Ke Log Bamboo Main Naag, Aloo, Butterfly Gai Dalke Kha Rahe

TrickDance
BambooBamboo: Kuki tribe
NaagRengma (Warrior Dance) Performed during Hornbill festival (1-10 Dec)
AlooAaluyattu: Konyak tribe
ButterflyButterfly: Zeliang tribe
GaiChangai: Changai tribe. Zeliang: Zeliang tribe. Modse: Ao tribe

(continued Nagaland and other states)

Odisha

Trick to Remember: Pua Khaya Dalkhai Danda Leke Ghum Raha Bhaga Nacha

TrickDance
Pua KhayaGotipua: Performed by young boys dressed as women to praise Lord Jagannath and Lord Krishna
DalkhaiDalkhai: Performed in Sambalpur region
Danda LekeDanda Nata: Performed in Kalahandi district
GhumGhumura (Tiger Dance) Performed in Kalahandi district
Bhaga NachaBhaga Nacha (Tiger Dance) Performed in Ganjam district. Chhau. Karma. Ranappa: Performed in Ganjam district. The dance is dedicated to Lord Krishna. Chaiti Ghoda dance

Sikkim

Trick to Remember: Chandni Sikkim Ki Zameen Pe Singh Ke Saath Ghante Bhar Se Yatra Kar Rahi Hai

TrickDance
ChandniChu-Faat: Performed by Lepcha tribe in Pang Lhabsol festival to honour God Kanchenjunga
Sikkim KiSikmari: Performed by Lepcha tribe to celebrate beauty of nature
ZameenZo-Mal-Lok (Yak Dance) Lepcha tribe
SinghSinghi Chham (Kanchendzonga Dance) Performed by Bhutia tribe during Pang Lhabsol festival
Ke SaathKagyed
GhanteGhantu
YatraYakcham: Performed in honour to yak during Losar festival. Maruni: Nepali folk dance of Magar community

Tamil Nadu

  • Kolattam Dance (stick dance): Women use sticks to create rhythmic beats and perform intricate movements.
  • Silambattam Dance: This is a martial art dance.
  • Oyilattam Dance: Performed in Madurai region.
  • Devarattam Dance: This dance is also known as "Dance of Gods".
  • Kudirai Attam Dance (Poikkal Kuthirai Attam Dance): Dancers wear a dummy horse structure while performing the dance.
  • Kummi Dance: Performed by women during Pongal festival (harvest festival).
  • Karadi Attam Dance (Burden Dance): Performed to worship Lord Murugan, the devotees carry decorated Kavadis on head.

Rajasthan

Trick to Remember: Raja Ganga Kal Ghoom Rahe The Chaar Thali Leke Susaini Ke Saath Lekin Khayalon Main

TrickDance
GangaGangaur: Performed to worship Mata Gauri (Lord Shiva's wife)
KalKalbeliya (Sapera Dance) Kalbeliya tribe (known as snake charmers)
Ghoom RaheGhoomar: Bhil tribe
ChaarChari: Performed by women of Gujjar community
ThaliTerah Taali: Kamar tribe
SusainiSuisini
KhayalonKhayal: Bhawai tribe

Gulabo Sapera is well known Kalbeliya dancer.

(continued Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand)

  • Mata Pe → Maimata: Kalol community.
  • Ghur → Garia: Performed during harvest festival (Spring season).
  • Le Jaunga → Lebang: A harvest dance that depicts how bamboo clappers catch insects. Cheraw: Lusal community. Sangrai Dance: Performed by Mog tribe in Sangria festival during Chaitra month (Bengali calendar year).

Telangana

Trick to Remember: Dhimse Gadi Gusa Lun Madhuri

TrickDance
Dhimsa SeDhimsa: Performed by women of Porja tribe in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
GadiLambadi: Lambadi tribe
Gusa LunGussadi: Performed by Raj Gond tribe during Dandari festival (Dussehra/Diwali festival)
MadhuriMathuri: Performed in Adilabad district. Bonalu: Performed during Bonali festival to honour Goddess Mahakali

Tripura

Trick to Remember: Biju Dadagiri Mata Pe Haq Hai Sang Ghar Le Jaunga

TrickDance
BijuBijhu: Chakma tribe
DadagiriHojagiri: Reang (Bru) community
Haq HaiHai Hak: Performed by Halam community to honour Goddess Lakshmi after harvest

Uttar Pradesh

  • Charkula Dance: Performed in Braj region of UP.
  • Raslila Dance: This dance depicts the scene from the life of Lord Krishna.
  • Nautanki Dance: A popular folk theatre form that combines music, dance, dialogue and narration.
  • Kajri Dance: It is performed during the rainy season in Bhojpuri region of UP and Bihar.
  • Ramlila Dance: A dramatic folk dance that re-enacts the life of Lord Rama.
  • Dadra Dance: A semi-classical romantic dance form that originated in Mirzapur district and is performed by both men and women.

Uttarakhand

Trick to Remember: Ashish Chanchlani Chora Hai Jhola Leke Dandi Rakh Chapa Chap Kar Raha Hai

TrickDance
ChanchlaniChanchari: Performed in Kumaon and Garhwal regions
ChoraJhora: Performed in Kumaon region
JholaChholia: A sword dance that depicts martial traditions of Kumaoni tribe
DandiTandi: Performed by men in half circles
Chapa ChapChhapeli: Performed in Kumaon region
Kar Raha HaiThadiya: Performed in Garhwal region. The dancers form semi-circle arcs by holding each other's shoulders

West Bengal

  • Gambhira Dance, Purulia Chhau Dance, Tusu Dance, Bhadu Dance, Ranpa Dance, Gambhira Dance.

Sangria Dance

The Sangria dance is a traditional Indian dance performed by the Mog tribal community on the occasion of the Sangria festival during the month of Chaitra of the Bengali calendar year.

Verified and Edited 2025

Verification date: 2025-12-15

OCR Artifacts Fixed

  • No stray column separators, mojibake characters, or broken line breaks found in body text.
  • Table separators (|) are intentional as part of the original 2-column trick tables and were preserved.

Factual Verifications

  • Andhra Pradesh: Verified Veeranatyam, Lambadi, Dhimsa, Kolattam, Bhamakalapam, Burrakatha, Bonalu, Butta Bommalu.
  • Arunachal Pradesh: Verified Rikhampada, Aji Lamu, Wancho, Buiya, Pasi Kongki, Chalo Loku, Bardo Chham, Lion and Peacock, Popir, Ponung, Yak Chham.
  • Assam: Verified Bihu (Rongali, Kati, Bhogali), Bhortal, Deodhani, Ankiya Naat, Ojapali, Jhumur, Bagarumba, Baidima, Bawang, Ali ai Ligang.
  • Gujarat: Verified Garba and Dandiya Raas (Navratri — Dandiya after aarti, Garba before aarti).
  • Chhattisgarh: Verified Pandavani by Usha Barle (Padma Shri 2023) and Teejan Bai (Padma Vibhushan 2019).
  • Himachal Pradesh: Verified Nati (Guinness World Record 9,892 dancers in Kullu).
  • Rajasthan: Verified Kalbeliya (Sapera Dance, snake charmers) and Gulabo Sapera.
  • Manipuri: Verified Lai Haraoba (Meitei tribe), Thang-Ta, Pung Cholom, Jagoi, Khamba Thoibi.
  • Sattriya & Pandavani cross-references noted.
  • Martial Art Dances: Lathi, Gatka, Silambam, Thang-Ta, Kalaripayattu, Thoda, Inbuan, Mardani Khel, Pari Khanda, Mallakhamba, Mushti Yudha — all match standard references.
